# Welcome to the brdrQ-Documentation page

<img src="./figures/icon_base_large.png" width="50" />

## Introduction

**brdrQ** is a QGIS plugin designed to align geometries with reference data. It helps users correct spatial discrepancies adjusting geometries to match reference sources using [`brdr`](https://github.com/OnroerendErfgoed/brdr).

## Installation

1. Open QGIS.
2. Go to `Plugins` -> `Manage and Install Plugins`.
3. Search for `brdrQ`.
4. Click `Install Plugin`.
5. Once installed, the plugin will appear in the plugin toolbar.

This plugin provides tools to align geometries to reference data.

## How to Read This Documentation

Start with the workflow choices below if you are new to brdrQ. Each tool page then starts with a short quick-start section for normal use, followed by a parameter guide and deeper notes for advanced workflows. Use [Q & A](qa.qmd) when you mainly want to interpret output fields, states, warnings, or integration choices.

## QGIS compatibility

`brdrQ` is currently maintained to run on both:

* QGIS 3 (Qt5 / `qgis.PyQt`)
* QGIS 4 (Qt6 / `qgis.PyQt`)

Compatibility wrappers are used in the plugin code for API differences (for example Qt enums and map-layer filter enums).

here you can find links to the different tools that are currently provided:

* [Feature aligner](featurealigner.md) - Feature-by-feature alignment with predictions
* [Autocorrectborders (BULK)](autocorrectborders.md) - Bulk alignment of your data to a reference layer
* [GRB Updater (BULK)](autoupdateborders.md) - Bulk alignment to latest GRB (Flanders - Belgium) based on predictions and provenance

## How-To Guides

Use how-to guides when you want to start from a concrete use case instead of a tool page.

* [Align a thematic layer to a local reference layer](howto-align-local-reference.qmd) - practical workflow for local reference data, direct output, and optional review.


## Workflow Choices

The tools can be used separately or in combination with each other. `RESULT_` and `DIFF_` layers are the primary output of the bulk tools; `CORRECTION_` is an optional review/workflow layer.

1. Direct output workflow: use [Autocorrectborders (BULK)](autocorrectborders.md) or [GRB Updater (BULK)](autoupdateborders.md), then consume the `RESULT_`/`brdrQ_RESULT_` layer and inspect the `DIFF_`/`brdrQ_DIFF_` layers in your own QA process.
2. Review workflow: enable the optional `CORRECTION_` layer, then use [Feature aligner](featurealigner.md) to review or update features with `brdrq_state` values such as `to_review` or `to_update`.
